EXPLICIT POSITIVE EHRHARD COVARIANCE COEFFICIENT

Source: GaussianEhrhardCoefficient.lean
Namespace: NegativeVotingEhrhard

Let p be an actual Gaussian cell mass in (0,1), q the standard Gaussian inverse
CDF, and phi its density. Define kappa(p) = 1 + p*q(p)/phi(q(p)).

CHECKED SCALAR BOUNDS
  kappa(p) >= exp(-4) / (2*(1 + q(p)^2));
  kappa(p) >= exp(-4) / (2*(1 + 2*log(1/p))) > 0.
If p >= 1/M and M >= 1, then
  kappa(p) >= exp(-4) / (2*(1 + 2*log(M))).

ACTUAL CONDITIONAL VARIANCE
For an arbitrary finite closed Gaussian polyhedron C with p = gamma(C) in (0,1),
and any vector v, gaussian_polyhedron_quantitative_variance_le proves

  (1/p) integral_C (<v,x> - M1/p)^2 dgamma(x)
    <= ||v||^2 - [exp(-4)/(2*(1+2*log(1/p)))] * (M1/p)^2,

where M1 = integral_C <v,x> dgamma(x). Thus the variance, mean, probability,
and coefficient all refer to the actual Gaussian measure. No assumed
isoperimetry, differentiability, covariance inequality, or coefficient bound
appears as a premise of this endpoint.

PROOF OF THE COEFFICIENT
At q(p)=-a <= 0, the exact gap identity is
  phi(a)-a*Phi(-a) = integral_(-infinity,-a] (-a-x)*phi(x) dx.
The first moment is obtained from mathlib's weighted Gaussian integrability
and the antiderivative -phi. Put delta=1/(1+a). On the literal interval
[-a-2*delta,-a-delta], the linear gap is at least delta and the density is at
least exp(-4)*phi(a). Integrating gives exp(-4)*delta^2*phi(a). The elementary
inequality (1+a)^2 <= 2*(1+a^2) yields the first bound. For q(p)>=0, kappa>=1.
An actual Gaussian Chernoff estimate bounds q(p)^2 by 2*log(1/p) when q(p)<=0.
This proves the logarithmic form. No additional Mills-ratio source was used.

VERIFICATION AND SCOPE
This module has 16 public declarations (15 theorems, one definition).
verify_ehrhard_complete.py checks the exact 17-file local source closure,
the pinned Lean/mathlib versions, a Lake build, and all 77 declarations in the
five new extension modules. The imported smooth Ehrhard endpoint has its own
transitive axiom audit. All audits permit only propext, Classical.choice, and
Quot.sound. EHRHARD_COMPLETE_VERIFICATION.json records the completed run.

These are classical Ehrhard and Gaussian localization facts formalized for the
research project. They are not claimed as newly discovered mathematical results,
and they do not alone constitute a proof of the negative-voting theorem.
